subject: Film & Cinema
title: Dogme 95: Stripping Cinema Bare
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Dogme 95: Stripping Cinema Bare.

hook.text: In 1995, two Danish directors wrote ten rules and dared filmmakers to follow them.

buildup.text: Lars von Trier and Thomas Vinterberg demanded handheld cameras, natural light, and no props.

discovery.text: The Celebration proved that stripping away everything could reveal raw emotional truth.

twist.text: Von Trier himself broke almost every Dogme rule in his later films.

climax.text: Dogme 95 was less a sustainable movement and more a creative dare that shook up cinema.

punchline.text: The strictest rules produced the freest films.

quiz.question: What did the Dogme 95 movement demand?
options: Handheld cameras, natural light, and no artificial props
